title: Nerve block injection
description: A nerve block is an injection of medication near a specific nerve or group of nerves to relieve pain. It can calm pain from conditions such as back or nerve pain, or provide numbing for a procedure. Your doctor cleans the skin and often uses imaging, such as X-ray or ultrasound, to guide the needle precisely to the target nerve. The injection usually contains a local anesthetic to numb the area and sometimes a steroid to reduce inflammation. You feel a brief prick and some pressure. Depending on the type, relief can begin within minutes and last from hours to weeks. A nerve block can reduce your pain, lower your need for other pain medication, and help you move and function more comfortably.
